In July staff proposed $65,000 for a second CSO truck and $135,000 for security cameras at city buildings and parks, citing theft, vandalism and higher insurance deductibles. Councillor Siemens asked why the library, which had twice raised security concerns, was left out; Councillor Susan Penner raised privacy and wanted committee discussion. Council deferred to a special meeting on August 11, 2026.
status_detail: The August 11 special/committee meeting is not in the public minutes, and no resolution allocating the grant appears in the minutes through Oct 6, 2026. Funds must be spent by March 31, 2027.
figures: $200,000 (Apr 7, 2026 minutes item 32); proposed $65,000 CSO truck + $135,000 cameras across 10 sites (Jul 21, 2026 minutes item 42); insurance deductible up from $2,500 to $10,000 in 2025 (Thiessen 1:22:18); city's earlier camera application to the Criminal Forfeiture Fund was denied (Thiessen 1:22:18).
reasons: study-first: wanted committee discussion of camera privacy and site choice (Susan Penner); study-first: wanted all candidate sites, including the library, compared (Jac Siemens)
public: The Jake Epp Library board had raised security concerns with council twice (per Siemens).
notes: Outcome of the Aug 11, 2026 meeting not found; check the Nov 2026 minutes or SteinbachOnline.

title: RCMP public and police safety framework consultation passed on as information
summary: The RCMP Contract Management Committee invited contract jurisdictions and the public to a consultation on a public and police safety framework. Council received it as information, with no submission of its own.
status_detail: Received as information (minutes item 11); no council submission recorded.

title: Residents' letter on people sheltering near Oak Crescent: CSOs already patrolling
summary: Residents (C.F. and A.F.) wrote about unhoused people at the shelter at Loewen Boulevard and Henry Street and the Oak Crescent pathway. The city manager reported the two CSOs had already visited, talked with the people there and found no safety hazards; council took the letter as information.
status_detail: Received as information; CSOs continue regular patrols and contact with unhoused people (city manager). Homelessness is covered in its own report.
reasons: already-doing-enough: CSOs handle these interactions daily (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: C.F. and A.F. raised safety concerns about the shelter and pathway (their letter).

title: 2026-27 RCMP priorities set without a council vote
summary: The new commander said the 2026-27 priorities (road safety, property crime reduction, intelligence-led policing and police visibility) were set after meeting the Steinbach Police Advisory Board and rural communities. Unlike every year from 2022 to 2025, no council resolution adopting them appears in the minutes.
status_detail: No priorities resolution found in the 2026 minutes through Oct 6, 2026.

title: RCMP report: full strength at last; mental-health calls up
summary: The new detachment commander (M.M.) reported all 18 municipal positions filled from September 21, 2026, steady calls for service, break-ins up from 78 to 91 year to date, arsons down from 11 to 2, Mental Health Act calls up from 251 to 311, and crime severity similar to Canada's and below Manitoba's. Councillors asked about Main Street racing, plain-clothes officers, e-bikes, overtime billing and private security.
status_detail: Delegation heard (minutes items 6-10). No motion; no targets set. Councillor J. Hiebert's question on which positions the city pays for was left for the commander to check.
figures: 18 municipal positions: 1 staff sergeant, 3 corporals, 2 GIS, 1 traffic, 11 general duty (minutes 6.1); calls 4,700 to date, 6,300-6,800 a year since 2021; break-ins 78 to 91; arsons 11 to 2; Mental Health Act calls 251 to 311 (transcript 0:05:50-0:13:10; minutes 6.3-6.4).
reasons: rcmp-job: residents should call police, not the mayor (M.M. (RCMP)); rcmp-cant-fill-positions: full strength is new and may not last (Michael Zwaagstra)
notes: RCMP officers identified by initials per project rule for delegates.

title: Overnight security contract awarded to Next Level after the first firm closes
summary: When Steinbach Security announced it would close on October 31, 2026, administration compared three quotes and an in-house option and recommended Next Level Servicing Corp., which took over the staff and equipment and runs a second patrol vehicle. Council approved it; Councillor Susan Penner said campaigning had shown property theft and community safety are residents' priority, and the mayor called it part of 'tiered policing.'
status_detail: Carried with no opposition heard (transcript). Contract from Nov 1, 2026 to at least Dec 31, 2027, retendered every three years. Resolution number pending (Oct 20 minutes not yet available).
figures: Next Level $380/night, $148,409 incl. PST for 2027; 2027 budget $150,000; Silver Star $137,901.60; in-house est. $176,933; Commissionaires $180,660.62; patrols cover 240-280 km a night (Oct 20, 2026 package, RFD 20260036).
reasons: rcmp-cant-fill-positions: RCMP hasn't consistently had a full complement (Susan Penner); cost: high policing cost and lack of RCMP make tiered policing attractive (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: Business community and developers reported the patrol made a 'night and day difference' (as recounted by the mayor).
notes: Seconder identified from the chair's 'Second by Councillor Siemens' 0:22:54 (speaker I replies 'Yes, sir').
